subject: Possible typos in reference manual 2.14 on multi-logit regression

messages.author: e1a47ce7e389b5dc
messages.subject: Possible typos in reference manual 2.14 on multi-logit regression
parts:
I'm reading the manual and something strikes me as odd, I'm wondering whether they are typos or I'm not understanding the model correctly. I copied the following text from the manual, on page 131:

Because softmax is invariant under adding a constant to each component of its input, the model is typically only identified if there is a suitable prior on the coefficients.
An alternative is to use (K 1)-vectors by fixing one of them to be zero. Sec- tion 10.2 discusses how to mix constants and parameters in a vector. In the multi- logit case, the parameter block would be redefined to use (K 1)-vectors
 parameters {
 matrix[K - 1, D] beta_raw;
}
and then these are transformed to parameters to use in the model. First, a trans- formed data block is added before the parameters block to define a column vector of zero values,
 transformed data {
 vector[D] zeros;
 zeros = rep_vector(0, D);
}
and then these are appended to beta_row to produce the coefficient matrix beta,
 transformed parameters {
 matrix[K, D] beta;
 beta = append_row(beta_raw, zeros);
}
See Section 41.7 for a definition of rep_vector and Section 41.10 for a definition of append_col. 

In the transformed parameters block, `zeros` are appended to `beta_raw` as one row, so `zeros` should be a row vector; but it's defined in the transformed data part as a (column) vector and populated with `rep_vector` which is also used to populated column vectors. What's going on here?

I ask because I copied the code and run it, the complier thrown me an error about appending column vectors using the `append_row` function. 

And the code used `append_row` but the last line is talking about `append_col`, this must be an typo I gather? :)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Possible typos in reference manual 2.14 on multi-logit regression
parts:
Thanks. Definitely a bug in that code---it wouldn't compile.
I created an issue comment and will fix in next manual.

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/2122#issuecomment-286202571

The vector of zeroes should be defined as

row_vector[D] zeros = rep_row_vector(0, D);

- Bob
